item.title: China's NEV share of new car sales continues to rise
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- New energy vehicles (NEVs) continued to gain ground in China's auto market in October, accounting for a larger share of new car sales, industry data showed on Wednesday. NEVs accounted for 64.3 percent of new car sales last month, up from 61.6 percent in September, while the cumulative share for the first 10 months climbed to 54.8 percent, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. In October, NEV output and sales reached about 2.02 million and 1.94 million units, respectively, both up by more than 13 percent year on year. ■

item.title: Russia, Ukraine resume talks after long hiatus, but breakthrough remains elusive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
* Zelensky said the discussions focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and mechanisms to ensure their long-term effectiveness, as well as steps toward de-escalation, adding that the main goal was to "truly bring peace closer." * Observers believe the trilateral talks could yield technical progress on less sensitive issues, such as humanitarian cooperation, localized ceasefires, safe corridors for grain exports and the establishment of a sustained dialogue mechanism. * Although the resumption of talks represents another attempt to resolve the conflict through diplomacy, the prospects for peace in the near term remain bleak. CAIRO/ABU DHABI, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- A new round of trilateral talks involving Russia, the United States and Ukraine entered its second day on Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The meeting marked the first trilateral talks among the three countries since February. Analysts say the talks have revived hopes for a diplomatic solution to the conflict, which has been dragging on for more than four years, and could pave the way for progress on practical issues, particularly humanitarian cooperation. However, they struck a more cautious note on the prospects for a comprehensive peace agreement, pointing to the lack of major breakthroughs in previous rounds of negotiations and the deep-rooted differences that continue to divide the two sides. RESUMPTION OF TALKS The delegations include several figures who have taken part in earlier rounds of negotiations, including Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and Ukrainian officials Rustem Umerov, head of the Foreign Intelligence Service, and Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office. The first day of talks concluded after nearly four hours of discussions, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky describing the session as "constructive and quite substantive." In a post on social media platform X, Zelensky said the discussions focused on security guarantees for Ukraine and mechanisms to ensure their long-term effectiveness, as well as steps toward de-escalation, adding that the main goal was to "truly bring peace closer." At a press conference following the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also described the first day of talks in Abu Dhabi as "very productive." Despite the positive assessments, statements from Moscow and Kiev ahead of the talks suggested that the two sides had different expectations of what the latest round of negotiations should achieve. Russian Permanent Representative to the United Nations Vasily Nebenzya said Monday that Moscow opposes a "freeze" in the Ukraine conflict that would leave existing security threats unresolved and create conditions for renewed escalation. Ukraine, meanwhile, has called for an end to hostilities, reliable post-war security guarantees, economic recovery and development, as well as progress on humanitarian issues. The U.S. objective is "to bring Ukraine and Russia together to discuss directly their postwar security concerns, proposals, and potential solutions," Kushner said in a social media post before the talks. "We hope these discussions will identify areas of common ground, advance practical solutions, and build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations," he added. However, previous rounds of negotiations have shown that identifying common ground may be easier said than done. Following two days of talks in Geneva in February, during which Russian, U.S. and Ukrainian delegations held a total of eight hours of discussions but failed to reach agreement on key issues, direct talks among the three sides remained largely suspended for nine months. POSSIBLE PROGRESS, CORE DIVISIONS Observers believe the trilateral talks could yield technical progress on less sensitive issues, such as humanitarian cooperation, localized ceasefires, safe corridors for grain exports and the establishment of a sustained dialogue mechanism. Ahmed Al-Janabi, a UAE political analyst, said the importance of the talks lay not only in the possibility of reaching an agreement, but also in reopening negotiation channels to discuss the most complex issues, particularly security arrangements, stopping the escalation, humanitarian files and the future of the disputed areas. However, reconciliation still faces three major obstacles and constraints, according to the analysts. Firstly, fundamental differences remain difficult to bridge. Russia and Ukraine hold sharply opposing positions on fundamental issues such as territorial sovereignty and security guarantees, making it unlikely that their differences can be resolved in just one or two rounds of talks. Secondly, the battlefield situation continues to shape the pace of negotiations. Russia is currently maintaining its offensive along the frontline, while Ukraine continues to launch long-range strikes against Russian territory. Both sides seek to gain leverage in negotiations by gaining the upper hand on the battlefield. Thirdly, external factors, particularly those involving the United States and Europe, can also affect the talks. Political developments in both regions have added further uncertainty to the conflict and its diplomatic prospects. Amid all these challenges, territorial issues remain at the heart of the disagreements between Moscow and Kiev. "So far I see no grounds to say that territorial positions have noticeably converged. Kiev proposes a ceasefire to begin with. For Moscow, a ceasefire must become part of the terms of a final settlement," said Vadim Kozyulin, chief researcher at the Institute of Contemporary International Studies of the Russian Diplomatic Academy. "Territorial issues may simply not be on the agenda, but solutions can and must be sought," Kozyulin added. PEACE WITHOUT GUARANTEE Although the resumption of talks represents another attempt to resolve the conflict through diplomacy, the prospects for peace in the near term remain bleak. Ukraine is not expecting significant results from the first round of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, David Arakhamia, chairman of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction, a Ukrainian political party, told the media. He nevertheless acknowledged that resuming negotiations after a prolonged hiatus was an achievement in itself. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, meanwhile, made clear in his remarks on the negotiations that Moscow would not agree to calls for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. Such statements from officials in both countries are consistent with analysts' assessments of the limited prospects for an early breakthrough. "This round of talks is not expected to yield decisive results. In the foreseeable short term, resolving this issue is a far-fetched goal," said Azza Hashem, managing director of the Cairo-based Al Habtoor Research Center. Despite some positive developments in recent times, "there is no indication that the underlying dynamics of the negotiations have changed," said John Herbst, senior director of the Atlantic Council's Eurasia Center. "Any realistic expectations for the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks should therefore be very modest," he said prior to the talks. Andrey Kortunov, a member of the Russian International Affairs Council, also expressed caution about the prospects for a comprehensive peace agreement. "It seems to me that it is still very far from a full-fledged peace. Although the negotiations have resumed, one cannot rule out the possibility of a new escalation in the very near future," Kortunov said. "I would like to hope that the conflict will eventually end, but no one can guarantee these timelines today," he added. (Video reporters: Wen Xinnian, Wang Hao, He Xinyuan, Wang Zecong; video editors: Liu Ruoshi, Zhang Yuhong.)■

item.title: China's import expo wraps up with record intended deals, global debuts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
SHANGHAI, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) concluded in Shanghai on Tuesday, with the value of one-year intended deals reaching a record high of 85.45 billion U.S. dollars, up 2.3 percent from the previous edition, according to Xiao Lu, an official with the CIIE Bureau. This year's expo attracted a record 4,142 exhibitors, and its business exhibition area reached a record 370,000 square meters. For the first time, the number of participating Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders exceeded 300. The six-day event also featured a record 485 exhibits making their global, Asian or China debuts, up from 461 last year. U.S. exhibitors had the largest exhibition area among participating countries and regions for the eighth consecutive year, occupying over 50,000 square meters. Free exhibition space for the least developed countries increased by 17 percent this year, enabling broader participation. First held in 2018 as the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, the CIIE is part of China's efforts to expand imports and offers global businesses a platform to showcase products and connect with Chinese buyers. Among the technological highlights this year, U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm showcased the world's first 6G terminal prototype outside a laboratory setting, while German engineering giant Bosch made the global debut of an AI-powered home climate control system that optimizes temperature and energy use. Consumer innovations also drew attention. Canadian sportswear brand lululemon made the global debut of a running vest designed for cold weather, set to launch first in China on Dec. 8. The CIIE also served as a platform for emerging innovators. This year's innovation incubation section featured 633 projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. The ninth expo brought together 51 trade delegations and over 700 sub-delegations, while the number of registered visitors exceeded 470,000, surpassing last year's figure, according to Xiao. China has remained the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years, importing more than 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) worth of goods between 2021 and 2025. The country's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for expanding imports and continuing to host the CIIE, underscoring the expo's role in China's broader opening-up agenda. With the CIIE set to hold its 10th edition next year, preparations are already underway, with 143 companies and institutions signed up for the 2027 edition and over 100,000 square meters of exhibition space already booked, according to the bureau. ■

item.title: American's decades-long bond with Chinese hometown leaves legacy of kindness
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
This file photo taken on Sept. 19, 2005 shows David V. Plymire in Huangyuan County, northwest China's Qinghai Province. (Xinhua) XINING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- In 1987, when David V. Plymire first returned to Huangyuan, the plateau county in China he had left decades earlier for the United States, locals were surprised that he still spoke the local dialect fluently. "I simply talked to myself in front of a mirror so that I wouldn't forget the dialect of my hometown," he later explained to a local journalist. Born in 1931 in the United States, Plymire spent his formative years with his family in Huangyuan County, now in northwest China's Qinghai Province, before leaving at age 18. Now, the 95-year-old regards the county as his only hometown. Though an ocean away, Plymire never stopped thinking about the people of Huangyuan. Between 1987 and 2016, he returned more than 20 times, helping improve local health care and education. To support the once-underdeveloped county, he donated over 30 pieces of medical equipment worth some 6 million yuan (about 895,500 U.S. dollars) to the Huangyuan County People's Hospital. The donation included a CT scanner worth 350,000 U.S. dollars -- a piece of equipment that no other county-level hospital in Qinghai possessed at the time. The procurement and customs clearance process for the large machine was cumbersome, and only after numerous setbacks did it finally arrive in Huangyuan in 2000. Standing before the device, Plymire bowed deeply. "This scanner must serve the people of my hometown well," he said in the local dialect. In 2002, Jia Chengwu, a neurosurgeon from Shenyang, capital of northeast China's Liaoning Province, was dispatched to Huangyuan as part of the country's efforts to promote large-scale development of the western region. There, he performed the county's first craniotomy on a migrant worker with a head injury. "Without the CT scanner donated by Mr. Plymire, which enabled a timely diagnosis of the worker's intracranial hematoma, I could not have completed that surgery," Jia recalled. "With this batch of donated hardware and the paired assistance from supporting doctors, the hospital became a well-known medical institution in the surrounding area." Huang Jiong, head of the hospital, said the CT scanner remained in service for 15 years until around 2015, benefiting more than 20,000 people. The equipment allowed doctors to quickly diagnose hundreds of critically ill patients suffering from cerebral hemorrhage, cerebral infarction and meningitis, securing precious time for surgical rescue and saving numerous lives, Huang said. In addition to donating medical equipment, Plymire also coordinated with foreign friends to teach English at local schools. His sister, Mary Ann Plymire, who was born and grew up in Huangyuan, funded the purchase of the county's first ambulance. In 1998, the Huangyuan county government awarded both of them honorary citizenship. At Mary's request, her ashes were brought back to the county after she died in 2016, allowing her to rest in peace in the place where she spent her childhood. The roots of their devotion trace back to their father, Victor G. Plymire, a missionary who arrived in China in 1908 and settled in Huangyuan in 1921. According to David's book depicting his father's life in Huangyuan, the senior Plymire dedicated himself to treating villagers free of charge with modern medicine. He also sheltered locals from a warlord's massacre in a self-built gospel hall in 1929 and provided relief to refugees from Gansu and Shaanxi provinces in the 1940s during the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. "I believe the father and son are remembered not merely for the medical donations and educational assistance, but more importantly, because they sheltered the common people during an extremely special and life-threatening era," said Huo De, a cultural scholar at the county's federation of literary and art circles. "This is the foundation of the local people's deep affection for them." Now, the hospital incorporates David's story into its orientation training for new employees and internal study sessions, keeping alive this legacy of cross-border goodwill. "David did not simply donate a few pieces of equipment. He has become a moral role model," Huang said. The example set by the Plymires has continued to inspire others to follow. Influenced by Plymire, Jia, now 74 and retired for many years, overcomes altitude sickness to regularly visit Huangyuan at his own expense to lecture, see outpatients, and perform surgeries at the hospital. He has also sponsored three local students from Huangyuan and its neighboring area, including a Tibetan pupil. "We should follow David's example and do more good deeds," said Jia. ■ This undated file photo shows David V. Plymire (C) and his sister Mary Ann Plymire (R) communicate with Yu Yaode, former director of Huangyuan County People's Hospital, at the hospital in Huangyuan County, northwest China's Qinghai Province. (Xinhua)

item.title: Xinhua think tank report highlights high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
This photo shows copies of the think tank report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation." (Xinhua/Jin Liangkuai) XI'AN, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A national high-level think tank released a report on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation in promoting open world economy on Tuesday. The report, titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation," was released by Xinhua Institute, a think tank affiliated with Xinhua News Agency, at the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 & the 4th Silk Road (XI'AN) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, capital of northwest China's Shaanxi Province. Consisting of three chapters, the report showcases the concrete practices of Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) cooperation in building an open world economy, analyzes the serious challenges facing economic globalization, and explains the contemporary significance of BRI cooperation in following the historical trend and opening broad prospects for the world economy. According to the report, high-quality BRI cooperation exemplifies China's commitment to opening-up as a fundamental national policy and to a mutually beneficial opening-up strategy. The report noted that BRI cooperation has consistently upheld the principles of extensive consultation, joint contribution, and shared benefits; embraced open, green, and clean cooperation; and pursued high standards, sustainability, and better lives for people. By steering economic globalization toward greater openness, inclusiveness, balance, and benefits for all, the BRI contributes Chinese approaches and insights to the building of an open world economy, it said. The report stated that the rise of anti-globalization sentiment, the spread of unilateralism and protectionism, weak global growth drivers, lagging governance, and uneven development are realities that must be confronted. At the same time, economic globalization reflects the objective requirements of the development of productive forces, and its historical direction cannot be reversed. Countries are more interdependent than ever, creating major opportunities to address global problems through openness and cooperation. Amid these changes, China's approach is to consider both domestic and international conditions, expand high-standard opening-up, and build global development partnerships. In this way, it seeks to turn challenges into a powerful impetus for an open world economy and realize a vision of inclusive development and mutual benefit for all, said the report. BRI cooperation keeps pace with the times, meets development needs, and responds to people's aspirations. It takes concrete action against decoupling, supply chain disruption, and bloc confrontation, using connectivity to remove barriers and facilitate economic flows, according to the report. At this new stage of history, BRI cooperation is moving from major corridors to extensive networks. Driven by digitalization and the green transition, it is deepening institutional opening-up and promoting collaborative innovation to make global development more balanced, inclusive, and sustainable, the report said. Looking ahead, the report stressed that BRI cooperation will provide stronger support for an open world economy, bring renewed vitality to global economic governance, reinforce the foundations of a community with a shared future for humanity, and open brighter prospects for world peace and development. The full report, comprising approximately 18,000 Chinese characters, was released globally in both Chinese and English through relevant websites, journals, social media, and other platforms. ■ A participant reads a copy of a report titled "Building an Open World Economy Through Belt and Road Cooperation," at the Belt and Road Forum for International Think Tank Cooperation 2026 & the 4th Silk Road (XI'AN) International Communication Forum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Nov. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Yibo)

item.title: China's long-term friendship policy with Cuba remains unwavering: China's top political advisor
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- China has unwaveringly adhered to the policy of long-term friendship with Cuba, and firmly supports Cuba in its just struggle against sanctions, blockade and foreign interference, China's top political advisor Wang Huning said when meeting with Cuban Minister of Foreign Affairs Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla in Beijing Wednesday. Wang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, added that China is convinced that the Communist Party of Cuba (PCC) will lead the Cuban people to new achievements along the path of building socialism. Wang said relations between the two parties and two countries of China and Cuba have reached new heights and taken on a new look under the strategic guidance of the two leaders, and steady progress has been made in building a China-Cuba community with a shared future. Rodriguez, also the special envoy of the PCC and the Cuban Government, Member of the Political Bureau of the PCC Central Committee, said that Cuba places Cuba-China relations high on its diplomatic agenda. He thanked China for supporting Cuba as it copes with an extremely complex situation and external unilateral coercive measures. Noting that the important consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries serves as a vital guide for advancing bilateral relations, Rodriguez said Cuba stands ready to work with China to jointly build a Cuba-China community with a shared future. ■

item.title: Chinese premier to visit Thailand, travel to Philippines for China-ASEAN summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-11
BEIJING, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- At the invitation of Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, Chinese Premier Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Thailand from Nov. 13 to 15, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Wednesday. At the invitation of President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. of the Philippines, the rotating chair of ASEAN, Premier Li will attend the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila from Nov. 15 to 16, the spokesperson added. ■

item.title: Book of Xi's discourses on poverty reduction, alleviation published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-10
BEIJING, Nov. 10 (Xinhua) -- A compilation of discourses by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on poverty reduction and alleviation has been published by the Central Party Literature Press and released nationwide. Compiled by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, the book brings together 55 important articles by Xi on poverty reduction and alleviation. Some of these works are made public for the first time. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core has placed poverty alleviation high on its governance agenda and regarded it as the bottom line task in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects. China has won a complete victory in the fight against poverty and accomplished the arduous task of eliminating absolute poverty, creating a miracle in the human history of poverty reduction. In the process, the country has blazed a poverty reduction path and formed an anti-poverty theory with Chinese characteristics. Xi's discourses on poverty reduction and alleviation represent an important theoretical achievement in China's poverty alleviation efforts and the latest achievement in adapting Marxist anti-poverty theory to the Chinese context. These discourses provide important guidance for consolidating and expanding the achievements in poverty alleviation and advancing rural revitalization across the board, promoting modernization that delivers common prosperity for all, and building a better world free from poverty and featuring shared prosperity. ■
